title: Data Leakage
description: The parent user may unintentionally share sensitive information (email, password, name, govt ID) during registration, leading to potential data leakage if the information is intercepted or misused.

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: The authentication service may store sensitive user information insecurely, making it vulnerable to unauthorized access or breaches.

title: Data Misuse
description: The authentication service may misuse the collected data (email, password, name, govt ID) for purposes other than intended, such as marketing or profiling.

title: Unintended Disclosure
description: There is a risk that the authentication service may unintentionally disclose sensitive user information to third parties without consent.

title: Data Disclosure from Authentication Service
description: The authentication service may inadvertently disclose personal data when storing parent account information in the MongoDB users collection, especially if the data includes sensitive information that is not strictly necessary for the operation.

title: Data Disclosure in MongoDB
description: The MongoDB users collection may expose personal data to unauthorized access or breaches, leading to potential data disclosure of parent account information stored within it.

title: Data Leakage
description: The authentication service may inadvertently expose sensitive user data (e.g., JWT tokens) to unauthorized parties during the transmission process to the parent user.

title: Insecure Data Handling
description: The parent user may mishandle the received JWT and user data, leading to potential exposure or misuse of sensitive information.

title: Data Misuse
description: The parent user may use the received data in ways that violate user privacy, such as sharing it with third parties without consent.

title: Legitimate User Data Exposure
description: The child user may inadvertently expose their parent’s email and password during the login process, especially if the device is shared or if the login credentials are stored insecurely.

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: The authentication service may store the parent’s email and password insecurely, making it vulnerable to unauthorized access or breaches.

title: Data Misuse by Service
description: The authentication service may misuse the parent’s email and password for purposes other than authentication, such as marketing or profiling without consent.

title: Data Leakage
description: The authentication service may inadvertently expose sensitive child profile information when generating JWTs, leading to unauthorized access if the JWT is intercepted or misused.

title: Insecure Data Handling
description: The child user may not handle the received JWT securely, leading to potential exposure of sensitive information if the JWT is stored insecurely or shared with unauthorized parties.

title: Data Misuse
description: The child user may misuse the received JWT to access unauthorized resources or perform actions that compromise the privacy of other users.

title: Linking of Child Profile Data
description: The act of sharing child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) by the Parent User may lead to linking threats, where the combination of these attributes could be used to identify the child or associate them with other data, leading to privacy implications.

title: Inadequate Information Control
description: Once the child profile data is received by the Child Profile Management process, there may be inadequate controls in place to ensure that the data is not misused or accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to potential information leakage.

title: Data Disclosure from Child Profile Management
description: The process of storing or updating child profiles may lead to the unintentional disclosure of personal data, either through explicit sharing or implicit metadata exposure during the data transfer to the MongoDB childprofiles collection.

title: Data Disclosure in MongoDB Child Profiles Collection
description: Once the child profiles are stored in the MongoDB collection, there is a risk of unauthorized access or data breaches that could lead to the disclosure of sensitive personal information.

title: Lack of User Consent
description: The Child User may not have provided explicit consent for their data to be shared with the Video Management Service, leading to potential legal and ethical issues regarding data privacy.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The Video Management Service may not manage personal data properly, leading to risks of data breaches or misuse of personal information.

title: Identified Information in Metadata
description: The metadata associated with video files may contain identifiable information, which could lead to the identification of individuals if accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Data Disclosure of Personal Data
description: The storage and retrieval of video metadata and files may lead to the explicit or implicit disclosure of personal data, especially if the data is not adequately protected or if access controls are insufficient.

title: Data Disclosure from Child Profile Management
description: The process of storing child search and watch history may lead to the unintended disclosure of personal data if the data is not properly anonymized or if access controls are insufficient.

title: Data Disclosure in MongoDB Child Profiles Collection
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection may inadvertently disclose personal data if proper security measures are not in place, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive child information.

title: Lack of User Consent
description: The parent user may upload videos without providing explicit consent for the processing of their personal data, leading to a lack of legal basis for data processing.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The Video Management Service may not manage personal data properly, leading to potential non-compliance with data protection regulations.

title: Lack of consent for data sharing
description: The video management service may stream videos to the child user without obtaining proper consent, leading to a lack of legal compliance and potential privacy violations.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The child user may not manage their personal data properly after receiving the video, leading to potential misuse or exposure of sensitive information.

title: Data Disclosure from Child Profiles
description: The child browsing data being shared from the MongoDB childprofiles collection may lead to the disclosure of personal data, either explicitly or implicitly, to the AI Recommendation Engine. This could include sensitive information about children's online behavior and preferences, which should be minimized according to the principle of data minimality.

title: Data Disclosure by AI Recommendation Engine
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may process and store the child browsing data in a way that leads to unintended data disclosures, either through the generation of insights that can be linked back to individual children or through inadequate data protection measures.

title: Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (P4) shares browsing data with third-party advertisers (EE3), which may include personal data that could be disclosed without proper consent or necessity, violating the minimality principle.

title: Data Disclosure by Third-Party Advertisers
description: The third-party advertisers (EE3) may use the browsing data received from the AI Recommendation Engine (P4) in ways that lead to unintended data disclosures, such as sharing with other entities or using the data for profiling without user consent.

title: Data Disclosure of Government ID Images
description: The authentication service (Process) may unintentionally disclose government ID images during the storage process, either through explicit sharing with unauthorized parties or through implicit means such as metadata exposure.

title: Data Disclosure of Stored Government ID Images
description: The file system (DataStore) may expose stored government ID images to unauthorized access, leading to potential data breaches or misuse of sensitive personal information.

title: Linkability Threat
description: The act of storing JWT in localStorage can lead to linkability threats if the JWT contains identifiable information that can be linked to a user’s actions across different sessions or applications.

title: Inaccessibility Threat
description: If the JWT stored in localStorage is not properly secured, it may be accessible to unauthorized scripts or browser extensions, leading to potential information leakage.

title: Data Disclosure Threat
description: The JWT stored in localStorage may be exposed to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing attackers to retrieve sensitive information from the token.

title: Linking of Child Data to Parent
description: The process of retrieving child history for parent review may allow the parent to link the child's data with other identifiable information, leading to potential privacy violations.

title: Inadequate Identity Verification
description: The parent user may not be adequately verified before accessing the child's profile, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information.

title: Data Misuse by Parent User
description: Once the child history is retrieved, the parent may misuse the information for purposes not intended by the system, such as discrimination or stigmatization.
